issue: scripts/analyze.py publish_reports staged both reports and then replaced each destination in turn with no rollback. If the second os.replace failed, binary-analysis.json from the new run stayed beside interface-inventory.json from the previous one.
finding: The two reports describe one capture together: the binary layout and the interface inventory are regenerated from the same read-only evidence and are consumed together. The destination admission already refuses aliases, duplicates and irregular files, but the publication itself was per-file, so an interruption left an inconsistent pair that no reader can detect.

change.capture: each prior file's bytes are read immediately before its replace
change.rollback: on any exception after the first replacement, every file this call replaced is restored (or removed if it did not exist before)
change.unchanged_behaviour: destination admission, staging names, umask mode, UTF-8 LF content and successful publication

runs.before: second replace raises -> first destination contains the new report, second keeps the old one
runs.after: second replace raises -> both destinations keep their prior bytes and no staging file remains

cases: a normal call publishes both reports
a failed second replace restores the first
a failed second replace removes a first publication that had no prior file

limits: This narrows the window in which a partially published pair exists; it does not make two filesystem renames atomic. It adds no analysis behavior and changes no report content.
